links.comparator_used: Models trained on MIMIC-IV and applied to the target hospitals without adaptation (baseline implied by the abstract), compared with Domain Adaptation and Inductive Transfer Learning using limited target-domain data
links.outcome: Discrimination (AUC and AUPRC) for mortality prediction in a prospective multicenter ICU cohort of 539 patients
links.effect: DA improved discrimination across all evaluated models; LightGBM had the largest AUC gain (p = 0.0010) and XGBoost the largest AUPRC gain (p = 0.0419). Random Forest reached 90.7% AUC with DA and 81.3% AUPRC with ITL. Domain-adapted models outperformed APACHE II (p = 0.0044) and SOFA (p = 0.0077).
links.quote: DA consistently improved discrimination across all evaluated models, with LightGBM showing the most significant gains in Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) (p = 0.0010), and XGBoost yielding the largest improvements in Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC) (p = 0.0419).

design_hint: local adaptation (domain adaptation/transfer learning) before deployment
